draft.title: Non-government organisations
card: A non-government organisation (NGO) is a group that is not part of any government. It works to improve people's lives rather than to make a profit.
NGOs raise money from donations, such as gifts from the public, and from sponsors, such as businesses. Some also receive grants from governments.

NGOs use this money to run aid and community projects that improve wellbeing. They often work at a local scale, directly with communities. Examples are clean water projects, schools and health clinics.
Oxfam and the Red Cross are NGOs. They are independent of governments and work with local communities in many countries, including in Asia and the Pacific.
draft.remember: NGOs are non-profit groups outside government that raise money and run programs to improve wellbeing.

a.q: Which description best fits an NGO such as Oxfam or the Red Cross?
opts: A group outside government that runs programs for wellbeing
A government agency that collects taxes to fund programs
A business that sells goods to earn profit for its owners
A government department that sets laws for other countries
a.why: An NGO is not part of a government and works to improve lives, not to make a profit. A government agency is the tempting wrong answer, because it also funds programs, but it is part of a government.
a.clue: Think about who runs the group and why it exists.

b.q: A group in regional Victoria collects donations from the public. It uses the money to build wells and a school in a village in Timor-Leste. Why is it an NGO?
opts: It is outside government and works to improve wellbeing
It receives all of its money directly from taxes
It aims to make a profit from the village it helps
It was set up and run by the Timor-Leste government
b.why: The group is separate from any government and uses donations to run projects that improve wellbeing. The taxes option is wrong because this group is funded by public donations, so its money does not all come from taxes. Some NGOs do get government grants, but that is not what makes a group an NGO.
b.clue: Look at who runs the group, where its money comes from and what it does.

a.best: A group outside government that runs programs for wellbeing

b.best: It is outside government and works to improve wellbeing
